b: For context. Ive known this person for about a year now and after we both fully talked about our backstories and whatever we have no idea what to talk about and he turns to other people where he clearly has more fun to talk to them. So I asked him if im just not an interesting person and he reluctantly said “no, absolutely not”

In general everyone I would call my friend in present or past would always talk to me less and less over time after the backstory was told, meaning i never got into a deep friendship and would lose all of my friends as soon as i’d be out of school.

A point that may have caused this is that i had depression, or something of the kind, on from primary and would simply stop doing things i used to love, i lost any interest in things around me and would use ,still do, my phone with doomscrolling and online gaming as a sort of distraction, even though it didn’t bring me joy of any kind.
Im starting to try new things again as in reading books and trying to find an interest i would be focused on for a longer time.

But as the title says i have lost any social skills that i had before i had my phase of depression or whatever it was, and because of this i still struggle today with any connection and interesting conversations as i lack the focus as well as prolonged concentration to listen all the time. I also lost any sense of social cue for jokes. F.ex. In a group one friend says something and another adds to the sentence with a funny comment which is practically impossible for me to think about in the moment. Which is what i envy about some people’s skills in a social setting.

So in hindsight. How do i become more interesting as a person and a conversationalist? And how would
I keep finding information to talk about with a friend? Or is it not possible to make any big changes with peoples view of me if they already created this image of me being boring and bland?
